items.title: docs(auth): correct OAuth client ID requirements for the Git credential helper
items.body:
## Description

Follow-up to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4264.

That MR said `glab` uses its own OAuth application, so users don't need to register one. That's only true on GitLab.com: on GitLab Self-Managed and GitLab Dedicated, `glab` needs an OAuth application and a `client_id` for the host (`oauthClientID` in `internal/oauth2/config.go`). Without it, the new `--web --setup-git-credential-helper` example fails.

This MR:

- Corrects the claim. `glab`'s OAuth application is not confidential, so there's no client secret, and on self-managed one application set up by an administrator serves all users.
- Adds the `glab config set client_id` step to the `glab auth login` example.
- Restores the `--setup-git-credential-helper` flag description to its non-interactive focus, and notes that interactive login already offers the setup.
- Condenses the "Git credential helper" section in `authentication.md` under one heading.

## Related issues

Related to #8701

items.title: docs(artifact-registry): correct the token exchange prerequisite
items.body:
## Description

The help of `glab artifact-registry status` and `get-token`, and their pages under `docs/source/artifact-registry/`, give two instance prerequisites: an EE instance on GitLab 19.1 or later, and token exchange enabled through the `gate_token_exchange_endpoint` feature flag.

The second one no longer applies. gitlab-org/gitlab!236798 added the endpoint in 19.1 behind that flag, and gitlab-org/gitlab!253385 removed the flag in 19.4. Up to 19.3 the endpoint answered 404 unless the flag was enabled ([`token_exchange.rb` at v19.3.0-ee](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.3.0-ee/ee/lib/api/authn/token_exchange.rb#L19-22)); from 19.4 it checks only `authenticate!` ([at v19.4.0-ee](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.4.0-ee/ee/lib/api/authn/token_exchange.rb#L19-21)), as it still does on `master`. So an operator following the help looks for a flag that does not exist.

This MR:

- States the prerequisite as "A GitLab Enterprise Edition (EE) instance on GitLab 19.4 or later." in the `Long` help of both commands, and regenerates the two pages with `make gen-docs`.
- Adds `TestStatus_HelpNamesNoRemovedFeatureFlag` and `TestGetToken_HelpNamesNoRemovedFeatureFlag`, which hold each command's help to that prerequisite and to no mention of the flag.
- Rewrites the comments of the three 404 tests to name each kind of instance that answers 404. Their assertions do not change.

I named a version rather than a flag, as the issue suggests, and 19.4 alone: on 19.1 the endpoint also required a permission that only an add-on purchase granted ([at v19.1.0-ee](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/v19.1.0-ee/ee/lib/api/authn/token_exchange.rb#L74)), so "19.1 to 19.3 with the flag enabled" would still be incomplete. Happy to add those releases back if you prefer.

## Related Issues

Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ops/artifact-registry/-/issues/1272

Related to gitlab-org/gitlab#601520, the rollout issue of the removed flag.

## How has this been tested?

- The two new tests fail against `main`'s help text, each on both assertions, and pass with this change.
- `go test -race ./internal/... ./cmd/...` with Go 1.27.3: 7178 pass, 20 skip, none fail.
- golangci-lint v2.15.0, the comment-overlap check, the `check_docs_markdown` linters and commitlint report nothing; `make generate`, `make gen-docs`, `make check-embed`, `make check-args` and `go build ./...` leave the tree clean.

## Screenshots (if appropriate):

<details>
<summary>Help before and after, from glab built on main and on this branch</summary>

`glab artifact-registry status --help` on `main`:

```plaintext
  Prerequisites:

  - A GitLab Enterprise Edition (EE) instance on GitLab 19.1 or later.
  - Token exchange enabled on the instance (the
    `gate_token_exchange_endpoint` feature flag).
```

On this branch:

```plaintext
  Prerequisites:

  - A GitLab Enterprise Edition (EE) instance on GitLab 19.4 or later.
```

`glab artifact-registry get-token --help` shows the same two blocks.

</details>

items.title: fix(cmdutils): make glab work in clones from an SSH subdomain, such as ssh.gitlab.gnome.org
items.body:
## Description

Repository commands failed with "none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitLab host" when the SSH remote was on the SSH subdomain of a configured host, such as `ssh.gitlab.gnome.org` for `gitlab.gnome.org`. glab only matched such a remote through `ssh_host`, and a scripted `glab auth login`, or one done before cloning, leaves that unset (#8707).

When an SSH remote host is neither a known host nor an `ssh_host` value, the resolver now maps `ssh.<host>` and `altssh.<host>` to a configured `<host>`. An explicit `ssh_host` still takes precedence. This applies both with and without a `GITLAB_HOST` override. The test that asserted the old behavior, added in !2924, now asserts the new one.

I limited this to the `ssh.` and `altssh.` prefixes rather than any subdomain, so a separate instance such as `staging.gitlab.com` or `dev.gitlab.example.com` is not mistaken for the configured host. Instances that use another naming scheme still need `ssh_host`.

Unchanged:

- HTTPS remotes, which are still matched literally.
- Other subdomains of a configured host, which are still skipped.
- `altssh.gitlab.com` when `gitlab.com` is not in the config, which is still skipped.

## Related Issues

Closes #8707

## How has this been tested?

New cases in `Test_remoteResolverSSHHostMappingEdgeCases`. These fail without the fix:

- an `ssh.` remote, with and without `GITLAB_HOST` set to the configured host
- an `altssh.` remote

These pass with and without the fix, and check that the match doesn't widen:

- `ssh_host` on another entry winning over the `ssh.` match
- another subdomain of a configured host
- an HTTPS `ssh.` remote
- `altssh.gitlab.com` with `gitlab.com` not configured

`make test-changed` and `golangci-lint run` pass, and the comment-overlap gate reports nothing for the changed files. In a clone of `GNOME/gnome-settings-daemon` (remote `git@ssh.gitlab.gnome.org:...`, `ssh_host` unset), `glab issue list` fails with glab 1.126.0 and lists the issues with this branch.
